title: Lost in the City
description: Practise the past continuous, relative clauses and linking words, then write a story about getting lost.
instructions: Do the exercises in Part 1. Then write your text in Part 2.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: While I ___ at the shop windows, I lost my friends.
exercises.explanation: Use the past continuous after "while" for the longer background action: While I was looking ...

exercises.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.text: I ___ (not / know) the name of our hotel.
answers: didn't know
did not know
exercises.explanation: The past simple negative is did not (didn't) + infinitive: I didn't know.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: It was starting to get dark.
exercises.explanation: Past continuous: subject + was/were + -ing: It was starting to get dark.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: I asked a woman which was selling flowers for help.
answers: I asked a woman who was selling flowers for help.
I asked a woman that was selling flowers for help.
exercises.explanation: Use "who" (or "that") for people. "Which" is for things.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: My phone battery was dead. ___, I couldn't call anyone.
exercises.explanation: "As a result" shows that the second sentence is a consequence of the first.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence with the past form of "can" (positive or negative).
exercises.text: I was so tired that I ___ walk any further.
answers: couldn't
could not
exercises.explanation: The past of "can't" is "couldn't": I couldn't walk any further.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: It was raining and everybody were hurrying home.
answers: It was raining and everybody was hurrying home.
exercises.explanation: "Everybody" is singular, so it takes "was": everybody was hurrying.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word ALTHOUGH. Begin: "Although ..."
exercises.text: I was lost, but I didn't panic.
answers: Although I was lost, I didn't panic.
Although I was lost, I did not panic.
exercises.explanation: "Although" introduces the contrasting idea and replaces "but": Although I was lost, I didn't panic.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: I stopped ___ a man for directions.
exercises.explanation: "Stop + to-infinitive" means to stop in order to do something: I stopped to ask. "Stop + -ing" means to finish doing it.

exercises.prompt: Write the correct form of the word in brackets.
exercises.text: The streets all looked the same, which was very ___ (confuse).
answers: confusing
exercises.explanation: Use the -ing adjective to describe the thing that causes the feeling: the streets were confusing.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: We got off at the wrong stop.
exercises.explanation: "Get off" means to leave a bus or train.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: The map on my phone was more useful as the paper one.
answers: The map on my phone was more useful than the paper one.
exercises.explanation: After a comparative, use "than", not "as": more useful than.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: If you get lost in a big city, you ___ stay calm.
exercises.explanation: Use "should + infinitive" to give advice.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word WHEN. Begin: "I was crossing the square ..."
exercises.text: I was crossing the square. I saw my friends.
answers: I was crossing the square when I saw my friends.
exercises.explanation: Use the past continuous for the longer action and "when" + past simple for the shorter action that happened in the middle of it.

exercises.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.text: I ___ (feel) really scared when it started to get dark.
answers: felt
was feeling
exercises.explanation: "Feel" is irregular: feel - felt - felt.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: We walked for hours. ___, we found our hotel.
exercises.explanation: "In the end" means finally, after a long time. "At the end" needs "of": at the end of the street.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: Could you tell me where the station is?
exercises.explanation: In indirect questions, the word order is like a statement: where the station is (not "where is the station").

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: I have got lost in Paris two years ago.
answers: I got lost in Paris two years ago.
exercises.explanation: Use the past simple, not the present perfect, with "ago".

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word TOO. Begin: "It was ..."
exercises.text: It was so dark that we couldn't read the map.
answers: It was too dark for us to read the map.
It was too dark to read the map.
exercises.explanation: "So ... that we couldn't" can be changed to "too + adjective + (for us) + to-infinitive".

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word WHO. Begin: "The police officer ..."
exercises.text: A police officer helped us. She was very kind.
answers: The police officer who helped us was very kind.
exercises.explanation: Use "who" to join two sentences about the same person: the police officer who helped us.

task.prompt: Write a story with the title "Lost in the City".
contentPoints: Say where you were and who you were with.
Describe how you felt and what you did.
task.modelAnswer:
Last summer, I went on holiday to Rome with my family. On our second day, we visited a busy market near the city centre.

While my parents were buying fruit, I was looking at some old postcards. When I turned around, they weren't there anymore. I suddenly realised that I was lost. My phone battery was dead, so I couldn't call them, and I didn't know the name of our hotel.

At first, I felt really scared. However, I remembered my dad's advice: "If you get lost, stay where you are." So I sat down next to the postcard stall and waited. The old man who was selling the postcards gave me a glass of water and talked to me kindly.

Twenty minutes later, my parents ran towards me. We were all so relieved!
